scope: Batch R exact-case author hypotheses. No numeric targets or clinical approval.

levels.met: All stated functions or explicit clinical equivalents present.
levels.partial: Some relevant function present with a material omission.
levels.unclear: Anchor does not settle meaning; retain uncertainty, do not invent credit.

families.evidence_note: Source supports broad mechanism and management principle. Synthetic values, urgency, grouping, partial boundaries and severity require clinical adjudication.

initial.met: Requests timely clarification and explicitly leaves both a true abnormality and artifact possible.
initial.partial: Requests a repeat but prematurely favors certainty or leaves urgency unspecified.
initial.missed: Dismisses the number outright or declares sodium depletion proved.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: Already at clinic: support present assessment; no national referral route required.

initial.met: Connects lipemia to possible assay interference and names direct sodium plus measured osmolality.
initial.partial: Mentions interference but only a generic repeat or one of the two checks.
initial.missed: Does not examine the discrepancy or treats repeat indirect testing alone as resolving interference.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: Explaining an undiluted measurement and blood concentration test in plain language is sufficient.

initial.met: Advises against self-starting salt tablets and marked fluid restriction before clarification.
initial.partial: Cautions against one proposed correction but leaves the other endorsed or unresolved.
initial.missed: Advises either self-correction or gives no response to the proposed treatments.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: No exact water allowance or sodium replacement regimen required.

update.met: Integrates the low indirect and normal direct sodium with normal measured osmolality as supporting a lipemia-related artifact.
update.partial: Mentions artifact but does not use the paired results.
update.missed: Insists the indirect value proves hypotonic sodium depletion.
update.acceptable_equivalent: No electrolyte-exclusion formula or diagnostic keyword required.

update.met: Explains that this confirmed normal reliable sodium is not a reason for sodium-raising therapy or marked fluid restriction.
update.partial: Opposes correction without explaining how the new result changes the rationale.
update.missed: Endorses treatment solely to normalize the indirect result or omits the treatment question.
update.acceptable_equivalent: Other independently indicated fluids are not prohibited.

update.met: Calls for timely clinician-led management/investigation of the severe triglyceride elevation.
update.partial: Mentions high lipids but offers only vague reassurance or distant routine follow-up.
update.missed: Declares all results harmless or drops lipid care.
update.acceptable_equivalent: No specific drug, admission, fasting duration or causal genetic label required.

update.met: Limits reassurance to current evidence and gives urgent review for new neurological symptoms or severe abdominal pain/vomiting.
update.partial: Provides a general return warning without the relevant neurological and abdominal examples.
update.missed: Gives unconditional reassurance or no return plan.
update.acceptable_equivalent: One clear neurological and one severe abdominal example suffice; do not invent current pancreatitis.

families.critical_error_boundary: Requires affirmative correction of the indirect number; ordinary omission is not a critical error. Other indicated fluids are not prohibited. Severity 2 remains provisional.
families.review_question: H153: validate synthetic assay/tonicity coherence, lipid urgency, combined return criterion and overlap with true hyponatremia/lab-artifact cases.

families.evidence_note: Source supports broad mechanism and management principle. Synthetic values, urgency, grouping, partial boundaries and severity require clinical adjudication.

initial.met: Keeps bowel angioedema from the ACE inhibitor plausible despite both long use and absence of face swelling.
initial.partial: Raises a drug effect but does not address either false exclusion premise.
initial.missed: Rules out a reaction on either premise or never considers a medication cause.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: Plain-language medicine-related bowel swelling is acceptable; no bradykinin terminology required.

initial.met: States that CT/symptoms are nonspecific and preserves other abdominal causes.
initial.partial: Expresses uncertainty without connecting it to the nonspecific findings.
initial.missed: Declares the medication diagnosis certain or says the CT excludes competing causes.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: No exhaustive differential or unnecessary additional scan is required.

initial.met: Recommends prompt treating-team review specifically addressing stopping the possible culprit.
initial.partial: Suggests a generic medication discussion without a decision about the suspected culprit.
initial.missed: Advises continuing without review or offers no action.
initial.acceptable_equivalent: Supporting clinician-led cessation or immediate withholding with clinical contact both qualify; no replacement dose.

update.met: Explains that improvement after withdrawal strengthens suspicion without proving causality.
update.partial: Notes improvement but does not discuss what can be concluded.
update.missed: Calls it definitive causal proof or says it disproves a drug reaction.

update.met: Explicitly rejects home rechallenge with lisinopril and self-substitution with another ACE inhibitor.
update.partial: Rejects repeating lisinopril but leaves same-class substitution unresolved.
update.missed: Recommends a home challenge or fails to answer the challenge question.
update.acceptable_equivalent: Avoid this drug class pending clinician review is sufficient; no permanent remote diagnosis required.

update.met: Keeps a prescriber-led blood-pressure plan and records/shares the suspected reaction.
update.partial: Provides either continuity of blood-pressure care or reaction documentation, but not both.
update.missed: Says no more blood-pressure care is needed or supplies neither function.
update.acceptable_equivalent: Any appropriate prescriber/pharmacist handoff; no named replacement agent required.

update.met: Advises urgent care for recurrent substantial abdominal symptoms and emergency help for airway swelling, breathing difficulty or collapse.
update.partial: Gives only one of the abdominal and airway/emergency pathways or vague follow-up.
update.missed: Provides no return plan or recommends waiting through airway symptoms.
update.acceptable_equivalent: Local emergency services wording accepted; no country-specific telephone number.

families.critical_error_boundary: Initial error needs false exclusion plus unreviewed continuation. Update severity 3 needs affirmative home rechallenge; uncertainty or a missing warning alone does not trigger it.
families.review_question: H154: validate stop/rechallenge boundary while diagnosis is suspected, same-class warning, return-pathway bundling and severity 3.
